features.evidence: 2026-07-15: (1) PERMISSION WALL — root cause of user-reported 'references and templates not proactive': plugin skill files live outside the user's workspace, so every Read was denied ('you haven't granted it yet'); relative links were never the problem, they resolve correctly. (2) VERSION TRAP — 1.0.0 was pinned while 5 commits shipped, so installed users could never receive the rebrand; bumped both to 1.1.0, added per-plugin CHANGELOG.md and a Release Checklist in CLAUDE.md. (3) Gated setup+migrate with disable-model-invocation (they write files); validate+score stay model-invocable. Token saving from gating NOT confirmed — `plugin details` still counts them in always-on. (4) LICENSE restored to verbatim MIT (GitHub reported 'Other' because of the appended notice); attribution moved verbatim to NOTICE. (5) CI: .github/workflows/validate.yml runs init.sh + `claude plugin validate --strict` (verified it needs no auth: clean HOME/empty env exits 0; broken manifest exits 1) plus a guard that fails if a marketplace entry pins version. features.name: Flexible harness scoring (adapted layouts)
features.description: Score a harness that keeps its own file names and its own wording, instead of only one that matches blvck-harness's. A .harness-map.json declares where the five concepts live; the same 25 checks then score it, deterministically and in CI. Discovery (the judgment) happens once via /blvck-harness:migrate's new adapt fork; scoring stays reproducible forever after.
features.evidence: 2026-07-15: PROBLEM — a repo with docs/agent-guide.md + .harness/features.json loaded ZERO files (loadHarnessFiles had a closed 7-name allowlist), failed all 25 checks, and hit the Math.max(1,...) floor: 20/100 exit 1. The tool reported 'no harness' about a harness that existed. Meanwhile migrate.md already said 'classify by role, never by matching a known layout' — the right stance existed but terminated at migrate. BUILT AS 3 STEPS, each verified before the next: (1) stable check ids + matched needle + kind through the primitives; verified 25 checks/25 unique ids, self-score still 100/100. (2) Split loadHarnessFilesAuto into solo/team adapters + resolution + per-concept routingNeedles; scoreHarness dropped its `layout` param entirely, dissolving the stateRoutingNeedles leak at :278-280 rather than adding a third branch. PROVED PURE: diffed pre- vs post-refactor JSON from `git show HEAD:` on 4 fixtures (solo/team/both-names/empty) — byte-identical scores, incl. the 'both instruction names + both tracker spellings' case where resolve-to-first-candidate could have silently dropped a file from allText. (3) The map: overlay semantics (unmapped concepts keep built-in names), shape normalization for foreign JSON field names, glob via existing listFiles, realpath containment. VERIFIED: tests/fixtures/foreign-harness scores 100/100 exit 0 with NOTHING canonical at its root — 6 of 25 points earned by declared synonyms (Kickoff, Acceptance criteria, Single task rule, Wrap up, .SHELLFLAGS). init.sh went 3 -> 5 steps; the 3 original invariants untouched and still green. ADVERSARIAL, all in init.sh: flat prose with every right word -> instructions 1/5, overall 68, exit 1 (structuredText still gates mapped files); a declared path that does not exist -> exit 1 EVEN AT 84/100 (mapErrors block independently — without that a typo'd map would have passed the 70 bar); 11 invalid-map shapes -> exit 2; parent-dir escape and symlink escape -> exit 2. TEAM-AS-MAP EQUIVALENCE: team layout re-expressed as a user map with layout:solo (globs doing all the work) scores identically to native team, 100/100 — the map is a real generalization of the layouts, not a parallel implementation that will drift. BUGS FOUND BY THE TESTS, not by review: (a) containment falsely rejected merely-missing files because macOS hands out /var/... while realpath gives /private/var/... — only surfaced under init.sh's mktemp -d, my earlier scratch run under /private/tmp masked it; fixed by resolving against the real root. (b) The fixture's own Makefile comment contained the literal 'set -e', so verification.failsFast passed on the built-in needle and the synonym test was vacuous; reworded. CORRECTED THE PLAN'S PREMISE: only ONE pair of checks is a true duplicate (:312/:298, identical hasFile predicate, now linked via sharedWith). :309 is a strict SUBSET of :286, not a duplicate — linking them would have made vocabulary wrongly transitive across checks whose needle sets genuinely differ. ADAPT FORK EXERCISED (2026-07-15, the one thing no unit test reaches): built an untuned foreign repo — .github/AGENT_NOTES.md, ops/backlog.json ({backlog:[{ref,label,detail,phase,needs}]}), notes/*-session.md, scripts/check.sh, plus notes/ideas.md as a decoy that is explicitly NOT a session log — and followed migrate.md's adapt path literally against it. Baseline: 'Unscored, 20/100'. Following the prompt's Phase 1 role table and Phase 3b rules produced a correct map FIRST TRY: 100/100 adapted, exit 0, 10 of 25 points earned by declared synonyms (Ramp-up, Ready to merge, One thread at a time, Sign-off, Snags, Where things stand, fresh clone, scripts/check.sh). The ideas.md decoy was correctly excluded by globbing notes/*-session.md rather than notes/*.md — the 'a file that fits no role is unknown, never guess' rule did real work. HONESTY RE-PROVED ON THIS REPO, not just the tuned fixture: (a) deleted the '## Sign-off' section while LEAVING its synonym in the map -> lifecycle.endOfSession fails, 96/100 — vocabulary cannot invent a concept; (b) the careless notes/*.md glob -> ideas.md becomes the handoff, state.handoffContent fails, 96 not 100, and the Resolution table names ideas.md so the mistake is visible rather than silent; (c) deleted the declared scripts/check.sh -> exit 1 with 'concepts.verification: "scripts/check.sh" does not exist'. NOTE: `/blvck-harness:migrate` itself was not typed — it is disable-model-invocation (correctly, it writes), so the command DISPATCH is still unexercised; what was tested is the prompt's rules, which is where the risk was. OBSERVATION worth a future look: one heading ('One thread at a time') was used as the synonym for both scope.oneFeatureAtATime and scope.boundary, so one statement bought two points. Defensible here — scope.boundary's built-in needle is the bare word 'scope', which is looser than the synonym — but the prompt gives no guidance against reusing one phrase across two checks. NOT DONE (recorded, not hidden): teamFindings reads disk directly, so adapted layouts get scoring but no hygiene findings; the Math.max(1,...) floor stays (removal flips pass->fail on unchanged input = 2.0.0).

features.name: Flexible pm vault scoring (configured paths)
features.description: blvck-pm's validate/score honor pm-os.config.md's ## Paths instead of hard-checking literal folder names, with role-based classification as fallback; /blvck-pm:migrate gains the same adapt fork. Fixes the setup/validate drift found while doing it.
features.evidence: 2026-07-15: REAL BUG FOUND (not in the original scope): setup.md:20 wrote the identity file as ABOUT-ME/about-me.md while ELEVEN other places read ABOUT-ME/CLAUDE.md — verified by grep: validate.md x2, setup.md:7, SKILL.md:22, references/agent-design.md:7, and all 7 agent archetypes. Every vault /blvck-pm:setup ever scaffolded failed its own validate on structure check #1. Invisible because setup.md:27 tells the model to 'run the validate checks on what you just built; fix anything failing' — it was silently repaired at runtime every single time, so the defect never surfaced as a symptom. Fixed setup.md:20 to state the rename explicitly (source template name != destination name, the precedent product-claude.md -> PROJECTS/<slug>/CLAUDE.md already sets); validate.md now reports a legacy about-me.md as a RENAME with a one-line git mv, never as missing identity, so pre-1.2.0 vaults are not told their identity file is gone. PATHS: pm-config.md's ## Paths described itself as 'machine-read by every pm-os workflow' but validate/score ignored it entirely and checked literal names, AND the template omitted ABOUT-ME/ while hardcoding 2 of its 3 entries — which is exactly why the drift had nowhere to be caught. Extended to the full role set; validate.md/score.md/SKILL.md/workflows.md now resolve through it with the ladder configured -> default -> classify by role -> unresolved+offer migrate. migrate.md gained the relocate/adapt fork and a `declare` plan action. VERIFIED: ./init.sh passes; all 3 manifests pass --strict; grep confirms no stale about-me.md destination remains (only the template source name and the deliberate legacy-detection lines). LIMIT STATED, NOT GLOSSED: blvck-pm has no validator script, so unlike feat-009 this adaptation is best-effort model behavior — no exit code, no CI coverage, 'discover once then score deterministically' does not transfer. A reproducible pm scorer is a separate project.

features.name: Vision -> Plan chain + completeness checklist
features.description: blvck-pm 1.3. Adds the missing top of the product chain and the gate that makes 'a complete plan' mean something. NEW: vision.md template + workflow (its own file, not a section of product CLAUDE.md, because vision changes yearly while product context changes constantly). REUSED: the plan layer stays prd/lightweight-spec/one-pager -- no plan.md is created, adding one would make users guess which document to write. NEW: per-document completeness checklists (PRD requires success metric, target user, first-release scope) shipped as adjustable defaults, not fixed rules. The gate WARNS and lets through, and records the override with a date -- plan completeness is arguable in a way that 'do the tests pass' is not, and a tool that blocks here gets abandoned. Also: output language becomes a config setting -- structural rules (conclusion first, numbers over adjectives) are language-independent, the banned-word list is not. English ships first.
features.evidence: 2026-09-04: blvck-pm 1.3.0. NEW FILES: templates/vision.md (46 lines) and references/completeness.md (93 lines). Vision is its own file, not a section of product context — it changes yearly while product context changes weekly, so co-locating means it gets edited away by accident. NO plan.md was created: prd/lightweight-spec/one-pager already are the plan layer and a fourth document would only make users guess which to write; the chain is closed instead by a 'Vision Outcome Served' field in prd.md plus a workflows.md rule that a PRD matching no vision outcome must say so (either the work is off-strategy or the vision is stale — both worth knowing before engineering). COMPLETENESS: default checklists for 9 document types; the gate warns and never blocks, and on override appends a dated '## Completeness' section to the document itself carrying the user's own reason ('no reason given' rather than an invented one). Explicit non-goals recorded in the reference: it does not judge quality, does not cross-check documents, does not run mid-draft. Overridable per vault with exactly three verbs (drop/add/skip); an unknown verb or type is a config error, because a typo'd override reads as configured and silently does nothing. LANGUAGE: pm-os.config.md gains '## Language' (default en) and voice.md splits into structural rules (hold in every language) and lexical rules (English only) — applying an English banned-word list to a Thai PRD produces the illusion of a style check. Language is configured, never inferred from what the user typed, because an inferred language changes between documents in one vault and makes anti-style.md unenforceable. DRIFT FOUND IN MY OWN WORK, before commit: setup.md scaffolds an intentionally-empty vision skeleton while my first draft of validate.md failed unedited template text with ❌ — every fresh vault would have failed its own validate on day one, the exact class of bug feat-010 fixed. Corrected: an unedited skeleton is ⚠️ 'scaffolded, not yet written — run the vision workflow'. ALSO FIXED (root cause of that class): setup.md's final step said 'run validate and fix anything failing', which is how the about-me.md defect hid for two releases; it now must REPORT every repair. Setup targets a 5-minute interview with working defaults, and is documented as the upgrade path for pre-1.3.0 vaults (no fifth command — the plugin promises four). VERIFIED: ./init.sh passes all 5 steps; all 3 manifests pass `claude plugin validate --strict`; every references/ and templates/ path named in SKILL.md, the references, and the commands resolves to a file that exists. LIMIT, UNCHANGED AND NOT GLOSSED: this is all model behaviour — no script, no exit code, no CI. Nothing here is verified by init.sh beyond JSON validity and the manifests. That is precisely what feat-012 exists to fix, and it is why the scaffolder ships before the validator.

features.name: roadmap.json + the first blvck-pm scripts
features.description: blvck-pm 1.4. Closes the gap that blvck-pm has zero executable surface while blvck-harness has 1,293 lines. NEW: roadmap.json -- one per product, unit is a BUSINESS OUTCOME bound to a metric, lifecycle idea -> validated -> planned -> building -> shipped -> MEASURED. The terminal state is 'measured', not 'shipped': that is what makes it a PM tracker and not an engineering one. Optional link field to blvck-harness feature IDs so the two plugins compose without duplicating. Deliberately NOT named feature_list.json -- same name, different unit, would imply the plugins are interchangeable. NEW: create-vault.mjs (non-interactive, --target) FIRST, because nothing can be tested until a vault can be produced without a human -- this is why the about-me.md bug survived two releases. THEN validate-vault.mjs (structure, placeholders, staleness, naming, declared-path existence, roster drift, checklist gaps) with --json and three-valued exit codes. NEW: pm-os.config.json alongside the existing .md (additive -- the .md is only removed in 2.0.0). NEW: fixture vault under tests/ + init.sh steps 6-7 including the adversarial set: a declared path that does not exist must fail, right-sounding prose must not pass the checklist, an empty vault must report unscored. Every workflow output gains a link to the roadmap item it serves -- that link is what turns 19 disconnected generators into one system.
features.evidence: 2026-09-04: blvck-pm 1.4.0. blvck-pm went from 0 lines of code to 3 scripts (vault-utils.mjs 446, create-vault.mjs 141, validate-vault.mjs 108) and init.sh went 5 -> 7 steps. ROADMAP: roadmap.json, one per product, unit is a business outcome bound to a metric, lifecycle idea/validated/planned/building/shipped/measured. 'measured' is terminal AND is the only status required to carry a result (date, value, verdict hit|missed|inconclusive) — that is the entire difference between this and an engineering tracker, and it is enforced in code, not prose. Not named feature_list.json on purpose: same name, different unit, would imply the plugins are interchangeable. IDs are out-YYYYMMDD-slug (date is the allocator, no shared counter to race); harnessFeatures[] links an outcome to blvck-harness feature ids — the two plugins link rather than share a tracker. SCAFFOLDER FIRST, as planned: create-vault.mjs is why any of this can be tested at all. CONFIG: pm-os.config.json added ALONGSIDE the .md (additive, nothing breaks); the markdown reader stays as a bridge and retiring it is 2.0.0. Resolution ladder json -> md -> defaults, with realpath containment (borrowed from feat-009's macOS /var vs /private/var lesson). SCORING IS LINEAR, unlike harness: 25 checks, overall = passed/25*100, so 0 means 0. harness floors each subsystem at 1 and reports 20/100 for an empty repo, a number that reads as a measurement and is not one; that floor is a known 2.0.0 item there and was simply not repeated here. THREE FINDINGS BLOCK REGARDLESS OF SCORE, each a broken promise rather than a weak vault: a declared path that does not exist, an unresolved {{PLACEHOLDER}}, a roadmap error. TWO BUGS FOUND BY THE TESTS, NOT BY REVIEW: (a) a fresh scaffold scored 72/100 and EXITED 0 — an untouched skeleton reading as a finished vault, which is precisely how the about-me.md defect hid for two releases. Fixed by making unresolved placeholders blocking, which turned the round trip into a real invariant: scaffold must exit 1, filled fixture must exit 0. (b) a roadmap item marked 'measured' with its result deleted scored 96/100 and exited 0 — the surrounding vault carried it over the bar. Fixed by making roadmap errors blocking. Neither was visible by reading the code. (c) a third, found by the fixture on its first run: the current-focus freshness regex looked for 'Updated:' but the template bolds it as '**Updated:**', so EVERY vault ever built reported 'carries no Updated line'. Dead check since 1.0.0. VERIFIED: ./init.sh passes all 7 steps; step 6 proves scaffold-exits-1 and filled-fixture-scores-100; step 7 proves four anti-gaming assertions (missing declared path -> 1, measured-without-result -> 1, unknown role -> 2, out-of-tree path -> 2, empty dir -> unscored + 1). All 3 manifests pass --strict. FIXTURE DATE HANDLING: current-focus.md holds FIXTURE_DATE and init.sh stamps today before validating — the freshness check is genuinely time-dependent and a hardcoded date would pass today and fail CI in a month, which would be the test rotting rather than the code. LINE HELD: no judgment in the script. It answers 'does the PRD name a success metric', never 'is it a good one'; the latter stays in validate.md, which is a prompt. Recorded as a rule in CLAUDE.md so the next session does not blur it. NOT DONE: the completeness gate from feat-011 is still unenforced by code — the script does not parse documents for their checklists, only the vault for its structure. Deliberate; document-level checking needs the per-type config resolved and is a bigger change than 1.4.0 should carry.

features.name: Interviewed agent team + agent-smith bundled
features.description: blvck-pm 1.5. The agent team stops being a fixed roster and becomes the answer to 'who would you normally have to ask?'. CHANGED: the 7 archetypes become structures in a catalog, not a default team; setup asks who the user consults when planning and maps answers onto archetypes, generating anything unmatched. NEW: lead-engineer archetype -- the roster today has no engineering lens at all (customer-voice, competitive-intel, business-analyst, board-executive, prototype-builder, blind-reviewer, research-analyst) and it is the first perspective named as the reason this feature exists. NEW: agent-smith copied into plugins/blvck-pm/skills/agent-smith/ -- a plugin may ship several skills; it forces the explicit tool and model budget the 7 archetypes lack entirely today, which is also what makes blind-reviewer's independence structural instead of prose. PREREQUISITE: .agents/ and skills-lock.json are untracked right now, so agent-smith exists only on one machine and cannot ship until that is resolved. Also requires allowed-tools: Read(${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/**) or it hits the same permission wall as feat-008.
features.evidence: 2026-09-04: blvck-pm 1.5.0. UNBLOCKED THE BLOCKER by vendoring rather than committing .agents/: agent-smith is now at plugins/blvck-pm/skills/agent-smith/ (SKILL.md + 3 references, 392 lines) so it ships with /plugin install. A plugin may hold several skills — blvck-pm now has two. Source is ntwrcht/blvck-skills (the user's own repo, so no licensing question); a header records that edits here do not flow upstream. Added allowed-tools: Read(${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/**) per feat-008's permission-wall lesson — without it every reference load is denied. NEW ARCHETYPE lead-engineer: the roster had NO engineering lens across seven archetypes, and it was the first perspective named when this direction was set. It answers rather than only asking — every gap carries the decision a competent engineer would make, marked Decided (any engineer calls it the same way) or Flagged (touches cost/timeline/scope, hard to reverse, or low confidence), which is feat-014's escalation rule prototyped in one agent before it becomes the general contract. BUDGETS: all 8 archetypes now declare tools + model, where before all seven carried only name and description — so the cost discipline that agent-design.md documents at length had nothing behind it. research-analyst -> haiku is the one that matters: agent-design.md fans out one worker per source above 3 sources, making it the only agent whose model choice reaches a bill. board-executive -> opus (one invocation, pure judgment). Read-only agents get Read/Grep/Glob; prototype-builder alone gets write and shell. INTERVIEW REWRITTEN from a stage-based recommendation to one question — 'when you are planning something, who do you normally have to go ask?' — with an explicit answer->archetype mapping table. Nobody can answer 'which agents do you want' before using the tool. 'Nobody, I work alone' is handled as the MOST informative answer, not an empty one: it means agents are replacing a team that does not exist, so lead-engineer + blind-reviewer are the floor with the reason stated. ENFORCEMENT, added beyond the original scope because a documented budget nobody checks is just advice: config.agentBudgets is a 26th check in validate-vault.mjs — an agent file missing tools or model fails, naming the file and the field. Fixture updated to match, still 100/100 (26/26). HONEST LIMIT STATED IN THE DOCS, not glossed: a tool allowlist cannot express 'read this file and no other', so blind-reviewer's independence is STILL carried by its instructions. Denying write access makes it structurally unable to contaminate the document under review; it does not make it unable to read a sibling review. agent-design.md now says exactly that instead of implying the budget solved it. VERIFIED: ./init.sh passes all 7 steps; manifests pass --strict; all 8 archetypes' frontmatter parses with both fields. NOT VERIFIED: the bundled agent-smith has never been loaded at runtime from an installed plugin — same untestable-by-CI gap feat-008 recorded, since `claude -p` cannot exercise allowed-tools. The fix is by analogy to blvck-pm's own SKILL.md, which was verified interactively.

features.name: blvck-pm 2.0.0 breaking changes
features.description: Everything that cannot land in a MINOR, done together and once. (1) pm-os.config.md -> pm-os.config.json: markdown bullets with parentheticals cannot be parsed reliably, and the file is documented as the one fixed name, so changing it is breaking by definition. The .json shipped alongside in feat-012; here the .md is retired. (2) The escalation rule in references/agent-design.md is rewritten: rule 4 today says agents must escalate decisions and never make them, which is directly opposed to agents closing gaps -- and which has no meaning for a solo founder who has nobody to escalate to. New rule: agents decide, flag the decision as an assumption with what would change it, and skip the flag for minor calls, where 'minor' is defined by three testable conditions the user can tune (touches cost/timeline/scope, hard to reverse, confidence below threshold). The flagged list becomes the agenda for the real meeting -- which is the stakeholder-gap reduction this whole direction is aimed at. (3) Any check whose tightening would flip pass to fail on unchanged vaults.
